BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to compel them; this resembles the statements that he is not a tyrant or keeper over them.
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r2.anchor: أي لست بمسلط عليهم تجبرهم على ما تريد كقوله تعالى وما أنت عليهم بجبار

BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce the word with ṣād to match the following ṭāʾ; others read sīn, and a third reading blends ṣād with zāy. The word originally relates to writing and means overseer or one who monitors a matter.
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r3.anchor: أكثر القراء قرأوا بمصطر بالصاد على القلب لمناسبة الطاء بعدها وقرىء بالسين على الأصل

BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib links the word to standing over and maintaining something, as in the Qur'anic descriptions of God as one who sustains each soul and the Prophet as no keeper over them.
BURSEVI:v10p323#2/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب : يقال سطر فلان على كذا أو تسطر عليه إذا قام عليه قيام سطر

QASHANI:88:17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:88:17/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:88:17/r2.claim: Reminding may benefit someone prepared to ascend toward God; whoever turns away and is veiled by effects from their cause faces the great fire, defined as punishment for absolute veiling across all levels of existence.
QASHANI:88:17/r2.anchor: عسى أن يكون فيهم مستعد يتذكر ويتعظ فيرتقي في السلم المنخلعة إلى جناب الحق لا من أعرض واحتجب بهذه الآثار

QASHANI:88:17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:88:17/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:88:17/r3.claim: The clause that the Messenger is only a reminder and not a controller is an interruption: his duty is to remind, not overpower or compel, as the cited verses also say.
QASHANI:88:17/r3.anchor: اعتراض أي: ما إليك إلا التذكير لا الغلبة والقهر

QUSHAYRI:v3p416/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p416/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p416/r22.claim: Muhammad is commanded to remind people; he is not their controller, and reminding them is the mission entrusted to him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p416/r22.anchor: أنت مذكر لست عليهم بمصيطر } . لست عليهم بمسلط ؛ فذكر - يا محمد - بما أمرناك

SULAMI:v2p393#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p393#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p393#3/r1.claim: The Prophet was sent to call people, not to guide them.
SULAMI:v2p393#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : لأنك بعثت داعيا ، ولم تبعث هاديا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Prophet's not being a controller as not being a tyrant, and says to forgive and pardon them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : لست عليهم بمسيطر يقول : بجبار فاعف عنهم واصفح

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the word as one who has power over them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3422#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه بمسيطر قال : بمسلط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r5.claim: The surah terrifies with the resurrection and contrasts punishment for the wretched with reward for the blessed, then rebukes people who ignore creation's evidence of God's oneness and capacity to resurrect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r5.anchor: اشتملت هذه السورة على تهويل يوم القيامة وما فيه من عقاب قوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r6.claim: Its purposes also include strengthening the Prophet in his call despite rejection and warning that rejecters return to God for recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p293/r6.anchor: وتثبيتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الدعوة إلى الإسلام وأن لا يعبأ بإعراضهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r1.claim: The imperative calls for continuing and persisting in reminder; its omitted object is supplied by the following statement that the Prophet is no controller over them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r1.anchor: فالأمر مستعمل في طلب الاستمرار والدوام . ومفعول ( ذكر ) محذوف هو ضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r2.claim: Innamā gives the reason for continuing despite inattention; its restriction reassures the Prophet that he must remind but is not responsible for producing their acceptance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r2.anchor: والقصر المستفاد ب { إنما } قصر إضافي ، أي أنت مذكر لست وكيلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r3.claim: “You are not a coercer over them” is an appositional restatement of the restriction's negative side; muṣayṭir means one who compels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r3.anchor: وجملة { لست عليهم بمصيطر } بدل اشتمال من جملة القصر باعتبار جانب النفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r4.claim: The word is pronounced with ṣād by most readers, with sīn by Hisham, or with ṣād tinged by zāy by Hamza.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r4.anchor: والأشهر بالصاد . وتقدم في سورة الطور : { أم هم المصيطرون } وقرأ بها الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r5.claim: The statement is reassurance rather than new information and is not abrogated by commands to fight; fighting followed a sequence of polytheist aggression and expulsion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r5.anchor: فلا نسخ لحكم هذه الآية بآيات الأمر بقتالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects using the verse to establish religious freedom within the Muslim community: one who leaves Islam is given three days to repent, then killed, or ostracized and treated as a belligerent if unavailable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p306/r6.anchor: فمن يلحد في الإسلام بعد الدخول فيه يستتاب ثلاثا فإن لم يتب قتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p307/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p307/r1.claim: “Over them” is fronted before its predicate to preserve the verse's cadence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p307/r1.anchor: وتقديم { عليهم } على متعلقه وهو ( مسيطر ) للرعاية على الفاصلة .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r8.claim: Muṣayṭir means domineering, coercively striving to control people with arrogant authority.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r8.anchor: أي قاهرا جاهدا لهم مع تكبر تسلطا عليهم، يقال تسيطر علينا فلان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r9.claim: Some readers pronounce the consonant with sīn rather than ṣād; Harun also gives an open vowel on ṭāʾ, a Tamim form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r9.anchor: وقرأ بعض الناس «بمسيطر» بالسين وبعضهم بالصاد، وقد تقدم وقرأ هارون «بمصيطر» بفتح الطاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r10.claim: The Arabic lexicon has no other words on this pattern besides musayṭir, mubayṭir, mubayqir, and muhaymin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p475/r10.anchor: وليس في كلام العرب على هذا البناء غير مسيطر ومبيطر ومبيقر ومهيمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r1.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to kill people or compel them to believe; the verse was then abrogated by the sword verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r1.anchor: أي بمسلط فتقتلهم وتكرههم على الإيمان ثم نسختها آية السيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r2.speaker: أبو رزين وأبو عبد الرحمن وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والحلواني عن ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the word with sīn; the meaning of “controller” was explained at 52:37.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p100#5/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين وأبو عبد الرحمن وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والحلواني عن ابن عامر بمسيطر بالسين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujahid, and others explain that Muhammad is not a tyrant over the people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وغيرهما: لست عليهم بجبار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that the Prophet is not one who forces people to believe.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: لست بالذي تكرههم على الإيمان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r4.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says he was ordered to fight until people profess God's oneness, after which their lives and property are protected except by due right and their reckoning belongs to God; this route includes his recitation of the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p388#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا: لا إله إلا الله

FARRA:v3p257/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p257/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p257/r11.claim: Musayṭir means one who has power or control.
FARRA:v3p257/r11.anchor:
إلا البعير.
وقوله عز وجل: لست عليهم بمسيطر (22) بمسلط، والكتاب (بمصيطر)

FARRA:v3p257/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p257/r12.speaker: القراء
FARRA:v3p257/r12.claim: The written form has ṣād, while the recitation uses sīn; reading ṣād would also be correct alongside the codex spelling.
FARRA:v3p257/r12.anchor: (المصيطرون ) : بالصاد والقراءة بالسين ، ولو قرئت بالصاد كان مع الكتاب وكان صوابا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p525#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p525#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p525#8/r1.claim: Musayṭir means one who has authority or control over them.

JISHUMI:v10p7389/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7389/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7389/r3.claim: Musayṭir means one who controls another by coercion; it derives from writing, since keepers and overseers preserve matters in writing.
JISHUMI:v10p7389/r3.anchor: المسيطر: المتسلط على غيره بالقهر له، وسيطر: تسلط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p746/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p746/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p746/r11.claim: Musaytir means one who dominates or compels them; the word is open-ta in the dialect of Tamim and may take an object there.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p746/r11.anchor: بمتسلط ، كقوله : { وما أنت عليهم بجبار }

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r9.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r9.claim: He interprets musaytir as someone with power or authority over them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r10.claim: He interprets musaytir as a tyrant or coercive ruler.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r11.claim: He interprets musaytir as a lord or master.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p262/r12.claim: The Messenger cannot force people to believe.

MUJAHID:v2p754/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p754/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p754/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet is not a tyrant over them.
MUJAHID:v2p754/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ لست عليهم بمصيطر ﴾ يقول لست عليهم بجبار

MUQATIL:88:10-26/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r12.claim: Muhammad is to warn Mecca's people, like earlier prophets, and has no authority as a king over them.
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r12.anchor: أهل مكة يا محمد { إنمآ أنت مذكر }

MUQATIL:88:10-26/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r13.claim: The command that Muhammad is not their master was later abrogated by the sword verse in Sūrat Barāʾa.
MUQATIL:88:10-26/r13.anchor: لست عليهم بملك، ثم نسختها آية السيف في براءة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p335#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p335#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p335#5/r1.claim: Musayṭir means one who compels or controls; the verse has a reading with ṣād by the Medinese, Basrans, Ali, and Asim.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p335#5/r1.anchor: بمسلط كقوله وما أنت عليهم بجبار بمصيطر مدنى وبصرى وعلى وعاصم

QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r2.claim: Qurtubi first reads the verse as denying the Prophet coercive authority to kill people, then says the sword verse abrogated it.
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r2.anchor: أي بمسلط عليهم فتقتلهم. ثم نسختها آية السيف

QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r3.speaker: هارون الأعور
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r3.claim: He reads musaytir with an open ta and records the plural form; this is a Tamimi dialect.
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r3.anchor: وقرأ هارون الأعور «بمسيطر» بفتح الطاء، و«المسيطرون». وهي لغة تميم

QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r4.claim: Musaytir means one who controls, oversees, and records; the word derives from satr, a line of writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:88:21-25/r4.anchor: وفي الصحاح: «المسيطر والمصيطر: المسلط على الشيء، ليشرف عليه، ويتعهد أحواله

NAHHAS:v5p213/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v5p213/r16.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet cannot force people back into faith.
NAHHAS:v5p213/r16.anchor: قال ابن زيد أي لست تردهم إلى الإيمان

NAHHAS:v5p213/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p213/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses bi-musayṭir as a tyrant or coercive ruler.

NAHHAS:v5p213/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p213/r18.claim: The word derives from saṭr, a line held within bounds; tasayṭara means to dominate, and sīn becomes ṣād before ṭāʾ.
NAHHAS:v5p213/r18.anchor: أصله السين مشتق من السطر لأن معنى السطر هو الذي لا يخرج عن الشيء

NAHHAS:v5p213/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r19.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p213/r19.claim: Some say the command is abrogated by the command to kill polytheists wherever found.
NAHHAS:v5p213/r19.anchor: وقيل إنها منسوخة بقوله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v5p213/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r20.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p213/r20.claim: Others say it is not abrogated: those who profess Islam are left to their condition, as the Prophet's report says their lives and property are protected after the testimony, subject to its due rights.
NAHHAS:v5p213/r20.anchor: وقيل ليست منسوخة لأنهم إذا أظهروا الإسلام تركوا على جملتهم

NAHHAS:v5p213/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p213/r21.speaker: جابر
NAHHAS:v5p213/r21.claim: Jābir transmits the Prophet's statement that he was commanded to fight until people testify to God's oneness, after which their lives and property are protected except by right and their reckoning belongs to God.
NAHHAS:v5p213/r21.anchor: عن أبي الزبير عن جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله

QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet cannot control or coerce hearts into belief, which remain under God's power.
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r1.anchor: فأنت لا تملك من أمر قلوبهم شيئا

QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r2.claim: Later jihad was meant to remove barriers so people could hear the message and avoid persecution for accepting it, not to force belief.
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r2.anchor: إنما كان لإزالة العقبات من وجه الدعوة

QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r3.claim: This repeated teaching frees the preacher from carrying the outcome: he must deliver the message regardless of response and leave results to God's decree.
QUTB-ZILAL:88:22/r3.anchor: كي ينطلق إلى أدائها كائنة ما كانت الاستجابة

RAZI:88:22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:88:22/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI:88:22/r1.claim: The word musayṭir means one who dominates or has power over them.
RAZI:88:22/r1.anchor: { بمسيطر } بمسلط ، كقوله : { يقولون وما أنت عليهم بجبار }

RAZI:88:22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:88:22/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:88:22/r2.claim: The Prophet was commanded only to remind; he was not appointed to kill people or coerce them into faith.
RAZI:88:22/r2.anchor: المعنى أنك ما أمرت إلا بالتذكير

RAZI:88:22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:88:22/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:88:22/r3.claim: In Tamim speech the ṭāʾ may be fatḥa because sayṭara is transitive there.
RAZI:88:22/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو في لغة تميم مفتوح الطاء على أن سيطر متعد عندهم

RAZI:88:22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:88:22/r4.speaker: جميع المفسرين
RAZI:88:22/r4.claim: The commentators say the command not to dominate was abrogated by the fighting verse.
RAZI:88:22/r4.anchor: ثم نسختها آية القتال ، هذا قول جميع المفسرين

RAZI:88:22/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:88:22/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:88:22/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the word was already discussed under “Or are they the controllers?”
RAZI:88:22/r5.anchor: قد تقدم عند قوله : { أم هم المسيطرون }

RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses musayṭir as one with power or control, like the descriptions in 50:45 and 10:99.
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { * بمصيطر } بمسلط ، كقوله : { يقولون وما أنت عليهم بجبار

RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r2.claim: In Tamim’s dialect the tāʾ is open because their verb sayṭara is transitive.
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r2.anchor: هو في لغة تميم مفتوح الطاء على أن سيطر متعد عندهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r3.speaker: all exegetes
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r3.claim: The Messenger’s role is reminder, not compulsion to faith or power to kill; commentators say the verse was later abrogated by the fighting verse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p145#2/r3.anchor: فأما أن تكون مسلطا عليهم حتى تقتلهم ، أو تكرههم على الإيمان فلا ، قالوا : ثم نسختها آية القتال

SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r1.claim: The common form and some of Qunbul's routes use ṣād; Hishām uses sīn, Khalaf colors ṣād toward zāy, and two forms are reported from Khallād.
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r1.anchor: العامة على الصاد، وقنبل في بعض طرقه، وهشام بالسين وخلف بإشمام الصاد زايا

SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r2.speaker: هارون
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r2.claim: Hārūn reads the word as a passive participle with fatḥa on ṭāʾ, since sayṭara is transitive; only a few forms occur on this rare pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r2.anchor: وقرأ هارون " بمسيطر " بفتح الطاء اسم مفعول؛ لأن " سيطر " عندهم متعد

SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r3.claim: The suggestion that Mujaymir and Mudaybir are diminutives is noted alongside the author's prior judgment that treating muhaymin as a diminutive was a grave error.
SAMIN-DURR:88:22/r3.anchor: وتقدم أنه خطأ عظيم، وذلك في سورة المائدة وغيرها.

STUDYQURAN:88:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:88:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:88:21/r1.claim: The Prophet's role is to remind; he is not responsible for others' faith or disbelief and cannot create faith in their hearts.
STUDYQURAN:88:21/r1.anchor: The Prophet’s mission is only to remind people of the truth. He will not be held responsible for the faith or disbelief of others

TAB-FULL:v24p342/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as “you are not a tyrant over them.”
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {لست عليهم بمصيطر} [الغاشية: 22] يقول: لست عليهم بجبار "

TAB-FULL:v24p342/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as leaving God’s servants to Him.
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {لست عليهم بمصيطر} [الغاشية: 22] أي كل إلي عبادي "

TAB-FULL:v24p342/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the no-compulsion command was later abrogated by commands to fight and monitor polytheists, while the duty to remind remains.
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إنما أنت مذكر لست عليهم بمصيطر} [الغاشية: 22] قال: لست عليهم بمسلط أن تكرههم على الإيمان

TAB-FULL:v24p342/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r4.claim: The Prophet says he was ordered to fight people until they profess God’s oneness, at which point their lives and property are protected except for a rightful claim, with their reckoning left to God; he then recited this verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا: لا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v24p342/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as meaning that Muhammad is not a tyrant over them.
TAB-FULL:v24p342/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {بمصيطر} [الغاشية: 22] قال: جبار "

TABATABAI:88:22-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:88:22-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:88:22-26/r1.claim: Al-muṣayṭir, originally al-musayṭir, means one who dominates; the verse explains that the Prophet is only a reminder.
TABATABAI:88:22-26/r1.anchor: المصيطر - وأصله المسيطر - المتسلط، والجملة بيان وتفسير لقوله { إنما أنت مذكر }

TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r3.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r3.claim: Al-Qummī says the Prophet is neither a keeper nor a scribe over the people.
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r3.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { لست عليهم بمصيطر } قال بحافظ ولا كاتب عليهم

TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r4.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet’s statement that people’s lives and property are protected once they profess monotheism, except for its due, while their account is with God; the Prophet then recites the reminder verses.
TABATABAI:88:22-26#2/r4.anchor: أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله فإذا قالوها عصموا مني دماءهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p318/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p318/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p318/r9.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who exercises control or domination.

TABRISI:88:17/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:88:17/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:88:17/r7.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who dominates another through coercion.
TABRISI:88:17/r7.anchor: والمصيطر المتسلط على غيره بالقهر له

TABRISI:88:17/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:88:17/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:88:17/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says muṣayṭir and mubayṭir are the only two words of this pattern in Arabic.
TABRISI:88:17/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: مصيطر ومبيطر لا ثالث لهما في كلام العرب

TABRISI:88:20-26/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:88:20-26/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:88:20-26/r5.claim: The Prophet cannot force faith into people's hearts; his duty is warning, preaching, and patient invitation to truth.
TABRISI:88:20-26/r5.anchor: لست عليهم بمتسلط تسليطا يمكنك أن تدخل الإيمان في قلوبهم وتجبرهم عليه

TABRISI:88:20-26/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:88:20-26/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:88:20-26/r6.claim: An interpretation takes the verse as a temporary ban on fighting later abrogated by jihad, but the sound view says no abrogation: jihad is not coercion and rejection is not the Prophet's responsibility.
TABRISI:88:20-26/r6.anchor: والوجه الصحيح أنه لا نسخ فيه لأن الجهاد ليس بأكره للقلوب

THALABI:v10p190#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p190#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is commanded to remind people, not to coerce their belief; the text says this ruling was then abrogated by the fighting verse.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r1.anchor: بمسلط جبار يكرههم على الإيمان، ثم نسخ ذلك بآية القتال

THALABI:v10p190#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r2.speaker: هارون
THALABI:v10p190#2/r2.claim: Hārūn reads musayṭir with fatḥa on ṭāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r2.anchor: وقرأها هارون بمسيطر (بفتح الطاء) وهي لغة تميم

THALABI:v10p190#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v10p190#2/r3.claim: One interpretation connects the exception to ‘remind’: remind your people except those who turn away and disbelieve, for the reminder will not benefit them.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r3.anchor: فذكر قومك إلا من تولى وكفر منهم، فإنه لا ينفعه التذكير

THALABI:v10p190#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p190#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation connects it to ‘you are not a controller’: you may fight until the one who turns away and disbelieves submits.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r4.anchor: لست عليهم بمصيطر إلا على من تولى وكفر، فانك تقاتله حتى يسلم

THALABI:v10p190#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p190#2/r5.claim: A third reading attaches the exception to what follows: ‘but whoever turns away and disbelieves, God will punish him.’
THALABI:v10p190#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو راجع إلى ما بعده، وتقديره: لكن من تولى وكفر

THALABI:v10p190#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p190#2/r6.claim: The greater punishment is the Fire, greater than worldly hunger, drought, killing, and captivity; Ibn Masʿūd's reading explicitly says God will punish the rejecter.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r6.anchor: وانما قال: الأكبر لأنهم عذبوا في الدنيا بالجوع، والقحط، والقتل، والأسر

THALABI:v10p190#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p190#2/r7.speaker: ابن جعفر
THALABI:v10p190#2/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in iyābah, but Abū Ḥātim rejects the form on grammatical grounds.
THALABI:v10p190#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء، قال أبو حاتم: لا يجوز ذلك

ASAD-NOTES:88:21#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:88:21#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:88:21#n6/r1.claim: The literal phrase means that the Prophet has no power over them.
ASAD-NOTES:88:21#n6/r1.anchor: Lit., "thou hast no power over them"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p475/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p475/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p475/r2.claim: Muhammad is not empowered to kill people or compel belief; the source says the fighting verse later abrogated this ruling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p475/r2.anchor: أي بمسلط فتقتلهم، وتكرههم على الإيمان، ثم نسختها آية القتال.

WAHIDI-QT:88:22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:88:22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to force people to believe; this preceded the command to fight.
WAHIDI-QT:88:22/r1.anchor: { لست عليهم بمصيطر } بمسلط تكرههم على الايمان وهذا قبل أن أمر بالحرب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:88:21-26/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:88:21-26/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:88:21-26/r3.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to compel people into faith; this was before he was commanded to fight.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:88:21-26/r3.anchor: بمسلط تكرههم على الإيمان، وهذا قبل أن أمر بالحرب.

ELMALILI:88:18-26/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r15.claim: The Prophet’s task is only to deliver and remind; he should not try to force people to think or compel them to believe.
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r15.anchor: tezkir ile iktifâ et de daha ziyade zorlama, zorla düşündüreceğim diye uğraşma

ELMALILI:88:18-26/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r16.claim: Being no overpowering master means the Prophet cannot compel their reflection, control their hearts, or make them adopt a belief as he wishes.
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r16.anchor: Zorla nazar ettirip düşündürecek, her istediğin şeyi yaptıracak, kalblerine hükmedip

ELMALILI:88:18-26/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r17.claim: The verse is supported by the statement that the Prophet does not guide whom he loves.

ELMALILI:88:18-26/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r21.claim: The next surah elaborates the lesson of these reflections by drawing attention to changes in time while explaining the final return to God.
ELMALILI:88:18-26/r21.anchor: Allah’a rücû‘âkıbetinin bir tavzîhi siyâkında zaman tehavvülâtına dikkati celb ile başlayan

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r1.claim: The word muṣaiṭir also has the reading musaiṭir; its etymology is unclear, though Jeffery connects it with s-ṭ-r, writing.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Wort – das auch musaiṭir gelesen wird (Muʿǧam, ad loc.) – ist etymologisch ungeklärt; Jeffery bringt den Ausdruck in Verbindung mit der Wurzel s-ṭ-r, „schreiben“

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r2.claim: Despite the uncertain etymology, the verse likely means what 50:45 says: Muhammad is not a coercive tyrant, so the basic translation is sound.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zumindest lässt sich jedoch sagen, dass der vorliegende Vers sinngleich mit 50:45

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r3.claim: Other passages describe Muhammad as a warner or his proclamation as remembrance while acknowledging that its effect is uncertain.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:22:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Auch an anderen Stellen wird in Verbindung mit der Beschreibung Muḥammads als „Mahner“ (muḏakkir) bzw. seiner Verkündigungen als ḏikr darauf hingewiesen oder zumindest implizit vorausgesetzt, dass die angestrebte Wirkung unsicher ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:23:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:23:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:23:anmerkung/r1.claim: The usual reading of ʾillā cannot mean Muhammad has power only over unbelievers, since verses 21–22 say he cannot compel his hearers to believe.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:23:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Vers kann nicht, wie es das gängige Verständnis von ʾillā nahelegt, bedeuten, dass Muḥammad über niemanden außer über die Ungläubigen Gewalt hat

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r1.claim: The closing section directly addresses the Messenger: his role is to warn, and he has no coercive power over his hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das Schlussgesätz beginnt mit einer direkten Anrede des Verkünders: Seine Aufgabe bestehe lediglich darin „zu mahnen“, ansonsten habe er keine Gewalt über seine Hörer

CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r2.claim: Earlier direct addresses to the Prophet occur only in short consolations at 93, 94, and 108; in group II, this address becomes integrated into broader literary contexts and a regular sura-ending feature.
CORPUSCORANICUM:88:21-26:kommentar/r2.anchor: Ähnliche Anreden an den Propheten enthalten zuvor nur die kurzen Trostworte Q 93, 94 und 108; in Q 88 und anderen Texten aus Gruppe II wird die Form der Prophetenanrede dann in übergreifende literarische Zusammenhänge integriert

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r1.claim: The Prophet must warn and convey revelation without coercion because faith and worship require inward conviction; other verses similarly limit his mission to conveying the message, not ensuring guidance (3:20; 16:82; 28:56; 42:48).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ resulüne, hiçbir baskı ve zorlamaya meydan vermeden insanları uyarmasını ve gerçekleri onlara yalnızca tebliğ etmesini emretmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r2.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r2.claim: Some exegetes say the no-coercion directive was abrogated; the author rejects this, arguing that even after fighting was allowed the Prophet did not force belief, while punitive action addressed harmful agitators.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:88:21/r2.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bu âyetin neshedildiğini yani hükmünün kaldırıldığını söylemişlerse de bize göre bu görüş isabetli değildir

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369#2/r1.claim: The verse is read with ṣād, sīn, or an intermediate zāy-like sound; Ibn Khālawayh says the articulation rationale was already explained in Sūrat al-Ṭūr.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ لست عليهم بمصيطر ﴾ يقرأ بالصاد والسين واشمام الزاي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r7.claim: These readers use ṣād in بمصيطر; Ibn ʿĀmir has a sīn report, Ḥamza shades ṣād toward zāy, and al-Kisāʾī has a sīn report.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم ﴿ بمصيطر ﴾ بالصاد

QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#1/r1.claim: The reading keeps sīn rather than emphatic ṣād, reducing emphasis while preserving the predicate meaning controller.
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical reading keeps sīn rather than emphatic ṣād, reducing the emphatic coloring

QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#2/r1.claim: An intermediate ishmām-like articulation colors the sibilant between ṣād and zāy, with little semantic shift.
QIRAAT-ER:88:22:4#2/r1.anchor: intermediate/ishmām-like articulation colors the sibilant between ṣād and zāy-like voicing

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p368#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p368#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p368#5/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses musayṭir as one who subdues or compels.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p368#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بمصيطر ﴾ قال بقاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r5.claim: “You are not a controller over them” means not a coercive ruler, comparable to “you are not a tyrant over them.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r5.anchor: لست عليهم بمصيطر: أي بمسلط، كقوله: وما أنت عليهم بجبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r6.claim: The majority read ṣād; variants use sīn, an emphatic z-like sound, or fatḥa on ṭāʾ, the last attributed to Tamīmī usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بالصاد وكسر الطاء، وابن عامر في رواية، ونطيق عن قنبل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r7.claim: The verb sayṭara is transitive, as shown by its passive form; few Arabic agent nouns share its pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p465/r7.anchor: وسيطر متعد عندهم ويدل عليه فعل المطاوعة وهو تسطر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r1.claim: “You do not control them” restates the warning's meaning: the Prophet cannot compel them, as another verse says he is no tyrant over them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r1.anchor: لست بمتسلط عليهم تجبرهم على ما تريد كقوله تعالى وما أنت عليهم بجبار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r2.claim: The majority read ṣād with kasra ṭāʾ; ṣād replaces the original sīn in a word from s-ṭ-r, to dominate.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بمصيطر بالصاد وكسر الطاء والأصل السين والصاد بدل منه فإنه من السطر بمعنى التسلط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r3.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r3.claim: Ḥamza's transmission colors the ṣād toward zāy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة في رواية بإشمام الصاد زيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r4.speaker: هارون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r4.claim: Hārūn reads with an open ṭāʾ, a Tamīm dialect; the verb is transitive in their usage, as the form tusayṭir shows.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p117#5/r4.anchor: وهارون بفتح الطاء وهي لغة تميم وسيطر متعد عندهم ويدل عليه قولهم تسيطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p411/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p411/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p411/r1.claim: The Prophet is to remind people, not exercise control by killing them or forcing them to believe; al-Baghawi says the fighting verse abrogated this rule.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p411/r1.anchor: [أي: عظ يا محمد] (1) {إنما أنت مذكر لست عليهم بمسيطر}

BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r1.claim: The Prophet is not a controller over them; al-Kisāʾī reads the sīn form and Ḥamza uses an imāla-like sound.
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r1.anchor: بمتسلط، وعن الكسائي بالسين على الأصل وحمزة بالإشمام

BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r8.claim: A report promises an easy reckoning to whoever recites al-Ghāshiya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:88:22-26/r8.anchor: من قرأ سورة الغاشية حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r7.claim: As this is an early Meccan sura when the Prophet was commanded to pardon, he is only a reminder and not an enforcer; he will soon gain authority over others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r7.anchor: وكان مأمورا إذ ذاك بالصفح قال : { إنما أنت مذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisai reads the word with sin, preserving its original pronunciation.

DURR:88:22/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r1.speaker: جابر
DURR:88:22/r1.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet read musayṭir with ṣād; al-Hakim graded the report authentic.
DURR:88:22/r1.anchor: عن جابر قال : قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «لست عليهم بمصيطر » بالصاد

DURR:88:22/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:88:22/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses musayṭir as a despot and says to pardon and overlook them.
DURR:88:22/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { لست عليهم بمصيطر } يقول : بجبار فاعف عنهم وأصفح

DURR:88:22/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:88:22/r3.claim: Qatada glosses the Prophet’s lack of control as not being a conqueror over them.
DURR:88:22/r3.anchor: عن قتادة { لست عليهم بمصيطر } قال : بقاهر

DURR:88:22/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:88:22/r4.claim: Qatada says all servants ultimately belong to God.
DURR:88:22/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { لست عليهم بمصيطر } قال : كل عبادي إليّ

DURR:88:22/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:88:22/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses musayṭir as one empowered to control them.
DURR:88:22/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه { بمصيطر } قال : بمسلط

DURR:88:22/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:88:22/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet is no tyrant over them; whoever turns away and disbelieves is left to God’s reckoning.
DURR:88:22/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد { لست عليهم بمصيطر } قال : جبار { إلا من تولى وكفر } قال : حسابه على الله

DURR:88:22/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:88:22/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:88:22/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says this directive was abrogated by the command to fight polytheists wherever found.
DURR:88:22/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس { لست عليهم بمصيطر } نسخ ذلك فقال : { فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم }

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r2.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet said he was ordered to fight people until they profess the oneness of God, after which their blood and property are protected except by right, and their reckoning is with God.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r2.anchor: عن جابر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r3.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticated Jābir’s report that the Prophet read the word “bi-muṣayṭir” with ṣād.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r3.anchor: عن جابر قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لست عليهم بمصيطر بالصاد

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “not a controller over them” as not being a tyrant, and advises pardon and forbearance.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {لست عليهم بمصيطر} يقول: بجبار فاعف عنهم وأصفح

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as meaning the Prophet is not a conqueror over them.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {لست عليهم بمصيطر} قال: بقاهر

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r6.claim: Qatāda also says all servants ultimately belong to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {لست عليهم بمصيطر} قال: كل عبادي إلي

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the phrase as “not one who has authority over them.”
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه {بمصيطر} قال: بمسلط

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r8.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as not being a tyrant; those who turn away and disbelieve will be reckoned by God.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد {لست عليهم بمصيطر} قال: جبار {إلا من تولى وكفر} قال: حسابه على الله

DURR-FULL:v8p495/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r9.claim: A report in Abū Dāwūd’s abrogation work says this verse was abrogated by the command to kill polytheists wherever found.
DURR-FULL:v8p495/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {لست عليهم بمصيطر} نسخ ذلك فقال: (فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم)

NASHR:v2p377#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r17.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p377#2/r17.claim: Hishām reads المسيطرون and بمسيطر with sīn.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r17.anchor: فرواها هشام بالسين فيهما. ورواه خلف عن حمزة بإشمام الصاد الزاي (واختلف)

NASHR:v2p377#2/r18.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r18.speaker: خلف عن حمزة
NASHR:v2p377#2/r18.claim: Khalaf from Ḥamza uses an imāla-like articulation between ṣād and zāy for both forms.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r18.anchor: ورواه خلف عن حمزة بإشمام الصاد الزاي (واختلف)

NASHR:v2p377#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r19.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v2p377#2/r19.claim: For Qunbul, Ibn Shanabūdh via al-Mubhij reports ṣād in both forms, a route also expressly recorded by al-Dānī.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r19.anchor: فأما قنبل فرواه عنه بالصاد فيها ابن شنبوذ من المبهج، وكذا نص الداني في جامعه عنه،

NASHR:v2p377#2/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r20.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v2p377#2/r20.claim: Ibn Mujāhid and Ibn Shanabūdh via al-Mustanīr report sīn for Qunbul in both forms.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r20.anchor: ورواه عنه بالسين فيهما ابن مجاهد وابن شنبوذ من المستنير.

NASHR:v2p377#2/r21.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r21.speaker: الجمهور من العراقيين والمغاربة
NASHR:v2p377#2/r21.claim: The majority Iraqi and Maghribi route for Qunbul has sīn in المسيطرون but ṣād in بمسيطر, as in al-Shāṭibiyya and al-Taysīr.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r21.anchor: ونص على السين في المسيطرون والصاد في بمصيطر - الجمهور من العراقيين، والمغاربة،

NASHR:v2p377#2/r22.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r22.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p377#2/r22.claim: For Ibn Dhakwān, Ibn Mihrān and Ibn al-Faḥḥām through al-Fārisī from al-Naqqāsh report sīn in both; Ibn al-Akhram and others also transmit this.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r22.anchor: وأما ابن ذكوان فرواه عنه بالسين فيهما ابن مهران وابن الفحام من طريق الفارسي عن النقاش،

NASHR:v2p377#2/r23.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r23.speaker: ابن سوار والجمهور عن النقاش
NASHR:v2p377#2/r23.claim: Ibn Sawwār and most transmitters from al-Naqqāsh report ṣād in both for Ibn Dhakwān; this is the Shāṭibiyya and Taysīr reading.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r23.anchor: ورواه ابن سوار بالصاد فيهما. وكذلك روى الجمهور عن النقاش، وهو الذي في الشاطبية، والتيسير.

NASHR:v2p377#2/r24.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r24.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v2p377#2/r24.claim: The mainstream reading for Ḥafṣ uses ṣād in both forms, supported by numerous authorities and adopted by al-Dānī from Abū al-Ḥasan.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r24.anchor: وأما حفص فنص على الصاد له فيهما ابن مهران في غايته، وابن غلبون في تذكرته،

NASHR:v2p377#2/r25.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r25.speaker: زرعان عن عمرو
NASHR:v2p377#2/r25.claim: Zurʿān from ʿAmr reports sīn in both forms for Ḥafṣ; other transmitters also report this route.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r25.anchor: بالسين فيهما زرعان عن عمرو، وهو نص الهذلي عن الأشناني

NASHR:v2p377#2/r26.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r26.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v2p377#2/r26.claim: Other routes for Ḥafṣ read المسيطرون with sīn and بمسيطر with ṣād; al-Dānī read this to Abū al-Fatḥ and it appears in several cited works.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r26.anchor: وروى آخرون عنه المسيطرون بالسين (وبمصيطر) بالصاد، وكذا هو في المبهج، والإرشادين،

NASHR:v2p377#2/r27.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r27.speaker: خلاد
NASHR:v2p377#2/r27.claim: Most eastern and western transmitters read both forms for Khallād with an imāla-like articulation between ṣād and zāy; the source says no contrary text is known.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r27.anchor: وأما خلاد فالجمهور من المشارقة، والمغاربة على الإشمام فيهما له.

NASHR:v2p377#2/r28.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p377#2/r28.speaker: الحلواني ومحمد بن سعيد البزاز عن خلاد
NASHR:v2p377#2/r28.claim: Al-Ḥulwānī and Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd al-Bazzāz transmit ṣād for Khallād; the excerpt begins another route but cuts off before naming its reading.
NASHR:v2p377#2/r28.anchor: والصاد هي رواية الحلواني ومحمد بن سعيد البزاز، كلاهما عن خلاد - ورواية محمد بن لاحق عن

ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r1.claim: Muhaymin means one who exercises authority, as in the statement that the Messenger is not a tyrant over them.

ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r2.speaker: الجمهور وابن عامر وحمزة وهارون
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r2.claim: The majority read with ṣād and kasra on ṭāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir, Qunbul's transmitter Nuṭayq, and Ḥafṣ's transmitter Zarʿān have sīn; Ḥamzah has an imāla toward zāy; Hārūn opens ṭāʾ, a Tamīm dialect.

ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r3.claim: Sayṭara is transitive, as shown by its inchoative form tasattara; this pattern includes only musayṭir, muhaymin, mubayṭir, and mubayqir.
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r3.anchor: وسيطر متعد عندهم ويدل عليه فعل المطاوعة وهو تسطر

ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r4.claim: The valley names Mujaymir and Mudyabir may be diminutives of Mujmar and Mudbar.
ABUHAYYAN:88:22/r4.anchor: وجاء مجيمر اسم واد ومديبر ،   ويمكن أن يكون أصلهما

ALUSI:88:22/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:88:22/r1.claim: This confirms the limit of warning: the Prophet is not a coercive ruler who can force people to do what he wants, as in 50:45.
ALUSI:88:22/r1.anchor: تقرير له وتحقيق لمعنى الإنذار أي لست بمتسلط عليهم تجبرهم على ما تريد

ALUSI:88:22/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:88:22/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:88:22/r2.claim: The majority read muṣayṭir with ṣād and kasrah on ṭāʾ; its original consonant is sīn, replaced by ṣād, and the root conveys domination.
ALUSI:88:22/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بمصيطر بالصاد وكسر الطاء والأصل السين والصاد بدل منه

ALUSI:88:22/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:88:22/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:88:22/r3.claim: The root saṭara conveys domination; saṭara ʿalayhi means that someone dominated him.
ALUSI:88:22/r3.anchor: فإنه من السطر بمعنى التسلط يقال سطر عليه إذا تسلط

ALUSI:88:22/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:88:22/r4.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI:88:22/r4.claim: Ḥamzah, in one transmission, reads with ṣād colored toward zāy.
ALUSI:88:22/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة في رواية بإشمام الصاد زاياً

ALUSI:88:22/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:88:22/r5.speaker: هارون
ALUSI:88:22/r5.claim: Hārūn reads with fatḥah on ṭāʾ; this is a Tamīm dialect, where sayṭara is transitive, as indicated by tasayṭara.
ALUSI:88:22/r5.anchor: وهارون بفتح الطاء وهي لغة تميم وسيطر متعد عندهم ويدل عليه قولهم تسيطر

BAGHAWI:88:22/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:88:22/r1.claim: He is not a controller with power to kill them or compel them to believe.
BAGHAWI:88:22/r1.anchor: لست عليهم بمصيطر } بمسلط فتقتلهم وتكرههم على الإيمان

BAGHAWI:88:22/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:88:22/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:88:22/r2.claim: The author says this ruling was abrogated by the verse of fighting.
BAGHAWI:88:22/r2.anchor: فتقتلهم وتكرههم على الإيمان . نسختها آية القتال

BAYDAWI:88:22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:88:22/r1.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who dominates or coerces them.
BAYDAWI:88:22/r1.anchor: لست عليهم بمصيطر بمتسلط وعن الكسائي بالسين على الأصل وحمزة بالإشمام

BAYDAWI:88:22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:88:22/r2.speaker: الكسائي وحمزة
BAYDAWI:88:22/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads with sīn, the original consonant, while Ḥamza reads with imāla-like rounding (ishmām).
BAYDAWI:88:22/r2.anchor: وعن الكسائي بالسين على الأصل وحمزة بالإشمام

BIQAI:88:22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:88:22/r1.claim: The phrase 'over them' restricts the Prophet's lack of control to those people; the preposition conveys domination.
BIQAI:88:22/r1.anchor: وأشار إلى القهر بأداة الاستعلاء فقال

BIQAI:88:22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:88:22/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:88:22/r2.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who dominates or controls; Biqāʿī adds that God will soon grant the Prophet authority over others.
BIQAI:88:22/r2.anchor: وأما غيرهم فسنسلطك عليهم عن قريب

BIQAI:88:22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:88:22/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BIQAI:88:22/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the word with sīn, following its original form.

IBNASHUR:88:22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r1.claim: The clause “you are not a controller over them” is an appositive elaboration of the negative side of the preceding restriction.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r1.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة القصر باعتبار جانب النفي الذي يفيده القصر

IBNASHUR:88:22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r2.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who compels or coerces; ṣayṭara also occurs with initial sīn, though ṣād is more common.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r2.anchor: يقال : صيطر بصاد في أوله ، ويقال : سيطر بسين في أوله

IBNASHUR:88:22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r3.claim: The word appeared in al-Ṭūr as well; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes the different recitations there and here.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r3.anchor: وتقدم في سورة الطور ( 37 ) : { أم هم المصيطرون }

IBNASHUR:88:22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:88:22/r4.claim: The majority read the word with initial ṣād.

IBNASHUR:88:22/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r5.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر
IBNASHUR:88:22/r5.claim: Hishām, transmitting from Ibn ʿĀmir, reads it with initial sīn.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r5.anchor: وقرأ هشام عن ابن عامر بالسين

IBNASHUR:88:22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r6.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR:88:22/r6.claim: Ḥamza reads with ṣād pronounced with a zāy-like quality.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r6.anchor: وقرأه حمزة بإشمام الصاد صوت الزاي

IBNASHUR:88:22/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r7.claim: The negative statement reassures the Prophet that he is not accountable for their continued disbelief, since he was not charged with coercing them into faith.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r7.anchor: فالخبر بهذا النفي مستعمل كناية عن التطمين برفع التبعة عنه

IBNASHUR:88:22/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects abrogation by fighting verses: combat became obligatory after a sequence of aggressions initiated by polytheists, including expelling Muslims, to secure them from oppression.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r8.anchor: ثم جاء وجوب القتال بتسلسل حوادث كان المشركون هم البادئين

IBNASHUR:88:22/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r9.claim: He rejects using this verse as a guarantee of religious freedom within the Muslim community, distinguishing that setting from relations with polytheists.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r9.anchor: ومن الجهلة من يضع قوله :  { لست عليهم بمصيطر } في غير موضعه

IBNASHUR:88:22/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r10.claim: He states that an apostate is asked to repent for three days and killed if unrepentant; if unavailable, Muslims must expel and treat the person as a combatant.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r10.anchor: فمن يلحد في الإسلام بعد الدخول فيه يستتاب ثلاثاً فإن لم يتب قتل

IBNASHUR:88:22/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r11.claim: He applies the same rule to a person who renounces Islam or denies a necessary tenet after its implication is explained, then persists without an acceptable interpretation or desisting.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r11.anchor: وكذلك من جاء بقول أو عمل يقتضي نبذ الإسلام أو إنكار ما هو من أصول الدين

IBNASHUR:88:22/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:88:22/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:88:22/r12.claim: The object “over them” precedes its complement “controller” to preserve the verse ending.
IBNASHUR:88:22/r12.anchor: وتقديم { عليهم } على متعلقه وهو « مسيطر » للرعاية على الفاصلة

IBNATIYYA:88:22/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet is not a coercive ruler who subdues people through arrogant domination.
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r1.anchor: ثم نفى أن يكون مصيطراً على الناس ، أي قاهراً جاهداً مع تكبر تسلطاً عليهم

IBNATIYYA:88:22/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r2.claim: The phrase tasyṭara ʿalaynā fulān is used in Arabic for someone exercising control over us.
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r2.anchor: عليهم ، يقال تسيطر علينا فلان ، وقرأ بعض الناس

IBNATIYYA:88:22/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r3.claim: Some readers pronounce the initial consonant as sīn and others as ṣād.
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r3.anchor: وقرأ بعض الناس «بمسيطر » بالسين وبعضهم بالصاد ، وقد تقدم

IBNATIYYA:88:22/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r4.speaker: هارون
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r4.claim: Hārūn reads muṣayṭar with fatḥa on ṭāʾ, a Tamīm dialect.
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r4.anchor: وقرأ هارون «بمصيطَر » بفتح الطاء وهي لغة تميم

IBNATIYYA:88:22/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r5.claim: The pattern has four Arabic active participles: musayṭir, mubayṭir, mubayqir, and muhaymin; named nouns al-mudaybir and mujaymir may be diminutives.
IBNATIYYA:88:22/r5.anchor: وليس في كلام العرب على هذا البناء غير مسيطر ومبيطر ومبيقر ومهيمن

IBNKATHIR:88:21/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r1.claim: Muhammad is to remind people of what he was sent with; his duty is to convey, while God will reckon with them.
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r1.anchor: يا محمد - الناس بما أرسلت به إليهم ، فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

IBNKATHIR:88:21/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others explain that Muhammad is not a tyrant over the people.
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وغيرهما : لست عليهم بجبار

IBNKATHIR:88:21/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad is not someone who compels people to believe.
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : لست بالذي تكرههم على الإيمان

IBNKATHIR:88:21/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r4.speaker: جابر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r4.claim: The Prophet says he was commanded to fight people until they profess God’s oneness; then their lives and property are protected except by due right, and their reckoning is with God. Ahmad, Muslim, Tirmidhi, and Nasa’i transmit this with the verse recitation; Bukhari and Muslim report it from Abu Hurayra without the verse.
IBNKATHIR:88:21/r4.anchor: عن جابر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا : لا إله إلا الله

IBNKATHIR:88:22/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r1.claim: Muhammad is to remind people of what he was sent with; his duty is to convey, while God will reckon with them.
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r1.anchor: يا محمد - الناس بما أرسلت به إليهم ، فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

IBNKATHIR:88:22/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others explain that Muhammad is not a tyrant over the people.
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وغيرهما : لست عليهم بجبار

IBNKATHIR:88:22/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad is not someone who compels people to believe.
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : لست بالذي تكرههم على الإيمان

IBNKATHIR:88:22/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r4.speaker: جابر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r4.claim: The Prophet says he was commanded to fight people until they profess God’s oneness; then their lives and property are protected except by due right, and their reckoning is with God. Ahmad, Muslim, Tirmidhi, and Nasa’i transmit this with the verse recitation; Bukhari and Muslim report it from Abu Hurayra without the verse.
IBNKATHIR:88:22/r4.anchor: عن جابر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا : لا إله إلا الله

KASHSHAF:88:22/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:88:22/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet is not a controller or master over them, as in the statement that he is not a tyrant over them (50:45).
KASHSHAF:88:22/r1.anchor: { لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُسَيْطِرٍ } بمتسلط ، كقوله : { وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ } [ ق : 45 ]

KASHSHAF:88:22/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:88:22/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:88:22/r2.claim: A Tamīm dialect pronounces the ṭāʾ open; the transitive verb “sayṭara” and their usage “tusayṭir” support this reading.
KASHSHAF:88:22/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو في لغة تميم مفتوح الطاء ؛ على أن «سيطر » معتد عندهم وقولهم : تسيطر ، يدل عليه { إِلاَّ مَن تولى }

MAWARDI:88:22/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:88:22/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:88:22/r1.claim: Al-Daḥḥāk explains musayṭir as one who has power over them.
MAWARDI:88:22/r1.anchor: أحدها : لست عليهم بمسلط ، قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI:88:22/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:88:22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:88:22/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains musayṭir as a tyrant.

MAWARDI:88:22/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:88:22/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:88:22/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains musayṭir as a lord or master.

MAWARDI:88:22/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:88:22/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:88:22/r4.claim: The point is that the Prophet is not a controller who can force them to believe.
MAWARDI:88:22/r4.anchor: ومعنى الكلام لست عليهم بمسيطر أن تكرههم على الإيمان

NASAFI:88:22/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet is not an authority controlling them, as in 50:45.
NASAFI:88:22/r1.anchor: بمسلط كقوله { وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ } [ ق : 45 ]

NASAFI:88:22/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:88:22/r2.speaker: المدني والبصري وعلي وعاصم
NASAFI:88:22/r2.claim: The Medinan and Basran readers, Ali, and Asim read “bi-muṣayṭir” in this form.

QURTUBI:88:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:88:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:88:22/r1.claim: The Prophet is not empowered to dominate them or kill them; the author says the sword verse later abrogated this ruling.
QURTUBI:88:22/r1.anchor: " لست عليهم بمصيطر " أي بمسلط عليهم فتقتلهم . ثم نسختها آية السيف

QURTUBI:88:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:88:22/r2.speaker: هارون الأعور
QURTUBI:88:22/r2.claim: Hārūn al-Aʿwar reads the word with fatḥa on ṭāʾ, as in al-musayṭarūn in al-Ṭūr 52:37; the form is Tamīm dialect.
QURTUBI:88:22/r2.anchor: وقرأ هارون الأعور " بمسيطَر " ( بفتح الطاء )

QURTUBI:88:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:88:22/r3.speaker: الصحاح
QURTUBI:88:22/r3.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines musayṭir as one who controls something, oversees and tends its affairs, and records its deeds.
QURTUBI:88:22/r3.anchor: وفي الصحاح : " المسيطر والمصيطر : المسلط على الشيء ، ليشرف عليه ، ويتعهد أحواله

QURTUBI:88:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:88:22/r4.speaker: الصحاح
QURTUBI:88:22/r4.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ derives the word from sṭr, since writing stays within a line; the text also gives the idiom sayṭarta ʿalaynā.
QURTUBI:88:22/r4.anchor: من معنى السطر ألا يتجاوز ، فالكتاب مسطر

QURTUBI:88:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:88:22/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:88:22/r5.claim: The verb saṭarahu can also mean to knock someone down.

TAB:88:22/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r1.speaker: author
TAB:88:22/r1.claim: Musayṭir means one who has authority over or control of a people.

TAB:88:22/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r2.speaker: author
TAB:88:22/r2.claim: The Prophet is neither their ruler nor a tyrant who forces them to do what he wants; he should leave them to God and His judgment.
TAB:88:22/r2.anchor: لست عليهم بمسلّط ،   ولا أنت بجبار

TAB:88:22/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:88:22/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the Prophet is not a tyrant over them.
TAB:88:22/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ يقول :  لست عليهم بجبار

TAB:88:22/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:88:22/r4.claim: Qatada glosses the verse as ‘leave My servants to Me.’
TAB:88:22/r4.anchor: عن قتادة لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ :  أي كِلْ إليّ عبادي

TAB:88:22/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:88:22/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses musayṭir as a tyrant.
TAB:88:22/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  بِمُسَيْطِرٍ قال :  جبار

TAB:88:22/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:88:22/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse was abrogated by later commands to fight and constrain polytheists, while the reminder itself remained un-abrogated, citing 51:55.
TAB:88:22/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  إنّمَا أنْتَ مُذَكّرٌ لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ

TAB:88:22/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:88:22/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:88:22/r7.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet was commanded to fight people until they professed God’s oneness; their blood and property were then protected except by right, with their reckoning left to God, and he recited this verse.
TAB:88:22/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «أُمِرْتُ أنْ أُقاتِلَ النّاسَ حتى يَقُولُوا

ITQAN:v2p338#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#3/r4.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who compels or dominates.
